newsitem.title: USA: Dell CEO sees "very good" PC demand.
newsitem.headline: Dell CEO sees "very good" PC demand.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Dell said that overall personal computer demands continues to be "very good" and that he is comfortable with current industry forecasts of 15 to 20 percent PC unit growth worldwide over the next few years.

Speaking at a Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Dell also said that the company is looking at entering the computer workstation business, although he pointed out that some of Dell's higher end personal computers using Intel Corp's PentiumPro processors can almost be classified as computer workstations.

Dell also said he does not see much of a threat to the PC industry from the low cost, scaled down network computer, which has been recently introduced by Sun Microsystems Inc and International Business Machines Corp.
"I don't see it replacing the fundamental architecture in the computer world," Dell said.
